currentPhase.label: Post-Migration Stabilization / Pre-Beta
currentPhase.summary: The desktop app is usable, but it is still carrying migration debt, UI parity gaps, and some legacy/runtime overlap that should be cleaned up before calling it beta.

beta.note: Only if pre-beta hardening criteria are broadly satisfied in practice.

stable.note: Only after beta proves reliable as the default daily-use experience.

whereWeAre: Core flows are functional, but some UI behavior, persistence details, and shell/runtime overlap still need hardening.
The priority is making the migrated app feel complete, consistent, and reliable rather than expanding broad new feature scope.
Legacy fallback still exists as a safety net, which means the desktop shell is not yet the unquestioned default experience.
whereWeAreGoing: Finish migration-recovery work until the current desktop runtime is clearly the primary experience.
Use pre-beta hardening to reduce overlap, fix regressions, and keep large files refactored while stabilizing behavior.
Enter beta only once daily-use workflows are reliable enough that the legacy fallback is optional instead of necessary.

milestones.title: Migration Recovery
milestones.goal: Re-establish parity for the core Electron-era UX in the current desktop app.
blockers: A few UI/layout bugs still only settle correctly after manual interaction or resize.
Some legacy/runtime overlap still makes ownership of behavior less clean than it should be.
Visual parity is improved but still not consistently at the historical standard across all views.
focus: Finish missing behaviors in header, sidebar, docking, popups, support flows, theme manager, language manager, and window chrome.
Remove obviously redundant or temporary migration paths where the new implementation already exists.
Close obvious parity gaps that still force users back into the classic/legacy fallback.
exitCriteria: Core desktop UX behaves close enough to the historical app for normal daily use.
Major parity bugs are no longer blocking confidence in the migrated runtime.
Remaining work is mostly stabilization and polish rather than missing baseline behavior.

milestones.title: Pre-Beta Hardening
milestones.goal: Reduce runtime overlap and make the migrated app reliable enough for beta.
blockers: Cannot start in earnest until migration-recovery issues stop forcing workarounds.
Large files and mixed responsibilities still need steady cleanup while behavior is stabilized.
focus: Refactor large files continuously so stabilization does not create new monoliths.
Fix resize/layout bugs, persistence bugs, interaction regressions, and restart-only recovery issues.
Ensure the main user journeys work without manual recovery steps or hidden fallback behavior.
exitCriteria: Core library, tools, themes, support, settings, and language flows work reliably.
Known issues are mostly edge cases or non-blocking polish items.
Major migration architecture decisions are no longer in flux.

milestones.title: Beta
milestones.goal: Make the desktop runtime the feature-complete primary experience for normal users.
blockers: Depends on pre-beta hardening being broadly complete.
Should not start while legacy fallback is still needed for core confidence.
focus: Treat the desktop shell as the default runtime, not as a side path beside legacy.
Collect and fix real-world regressions from wider daily use.
Continue UX polish and structural cleanup without destabilizing core flows.
startCriteria: Core library browsing, emulators, support, themes, languages, tools, and settings work reliably.
Main UI/UX parity is close enough that legacy/classic is optional, not required.
The desktop runtime is clearly the preferred experience for normal use.

milestones.title: Stable
milestones.goal: Make the desktop app the default recommended experience with no major fallback dependency.
blockers: Requires beta to prove daily-use reliability over time.
Requires cross-platform and persistence quality to be consistently strong.
focus: Keep the release boring in the good way: reliable persistence, launches, downloads, updates, and settings.
Treat cross-platform behavior and shell integration as part of release quality, not follow-up work.
Focus future updates on measured improvements rather than core recovery.
startCriteria: No major workflow requires the legacy fallback.
Persistent data, downloads, launching, and settings survive restart cleanly.
Window behavior, responsiveness, and shell integration are consistent across supported setups.

betaDefinition: Legacy fallback is optional instead of required.
Remaining issues are mostly edge cases or polish.
stableDefinition: No major workflow depends on legacy fallback.
Reliability and persistence are strong enough that updates are incremental, not recovery-oriented.
futureUpdateTracks: Parity improvements where the historical UX still matters

history.title: Roadmap baseline captured
history.summary: Defined current phase, milestone gates, beta/stable meaning, and near-term priorities in repo notes and dashboard data.

history.title: Language manager stabilization continued
history.summary: Improved live edit visibility, language card selection, style preset management, and initial layout/scroll fixes.

history.title: Runtime cleanup resumed
history.summary: Started splitting language-manager runtime responsibilities back into feature-folder modules instead of growing one large runtime file.

nearTermTasks: Keep shrinking legacy bootstrap/runtime responsibilities once migrated replacements are proven.
Review large files during normal work and split them into feature-folder modules early.
Verify installer, protocol handling, persistence, and resource-download flows after major changes.
Treat restart-only, resize-only, and manual-interaction-only bugs as high-priority stabilization issues.
